claims.exact_statement: For b exchangeable daughter unsafe indicators with marginal epsilon, the sharp one-division probability of at least one unsafe daughter is in [epsilon, min(1,b*epsilon)].
assumptions: b is a fixed number of daughter slots
claims.status: internally derived exact Frechet/first-moment bound; standard; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary sharp dependence bounds; not a new branching theorem.
claims.costs: No computation. Empirical use requires paired daughter fate classification.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the stated fixed-b exchangeable law and marginal would falsify the algebraic claim.
claims.next_gate: Estimate the count of unsafe daughters per division rather than only the pooled single-cell marginal.

claims.exact_statement: If a full b-ary safe progenitor tree is forced through T divisions and every daughter has conditional unsafe marginal epsilon given the full prior all-safe history, then the sharp probability of no unsafe fate lies between max(0,1-b*epsilon)^H and (1-epsilon)^H, H=(b^T-1)/(b-1).
assumptions: Each safe parent divides once per generation
exactly b daughter slots per division
conditional marginal epsilon holds after every prior all-safe history
unsafe fate is a first-hit failure
claims.status: internally derived sharp finite-horizon bound under conditional-history interface; not biological validation
claims.novelty_boundary: Repeated sharp one-family Fréchet bounds plus chain rule; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Need a safe-path division cap/tree-depth horizon and conditional fate marginals; full-tree experiment cost grows with potential lineage count H.
claims.falsifier: Violation of the conditional marginal, exact full-tree, or offspring-cap assumptions invalidates the formula as a biological bound.
claims.next_gate: For a capped real system, measure safe quiescence/death and replace the full-tree assumption with its actual at-risk division bound.

claims.exact_statement: Under a one-type Galton-Watson process with exchangeable within-family offspring count K in {0,...,b}, mean mu=bp, and independent parent-family offspring vectors, the sharp T-generation survival interval over all admissible offspring laws is 1-G_max^T(0) <= P(Z_T>0) <= 1-G_min^T(0), where G_max(z)=1-p+p*z^b and G_min is the nearest-integer mean law on floor(mu),ceil(mu).
assumptions: fixed or generation-wise admissible mean mu
claims.status: internally derived via standard PGF recursion and convex order; sharp under stated assumptions; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Galton-Watson/convex-order result; lineage literature already represents joint offspring laws. No novelty or priority claim.
claims.costs: Empirical prediction requires the family-level offspring count law, not only state transition marginals; sequencing, imaging, and clone-level replication are charged.
claims.falsifier: The algebraic statement is falsified by a law satisfying its constraints but outside the recursively computed interval; biological use fails if inter-parent dependence or density feedback is material and omitted.
claims.next_gate: Fit the offspring PGF and test held-out clone persistence under the intervention; include clone-level latent effects if parent families are dependent.

claims.exact_statement: For b=3, two exchangeable offspring-count laws (1,3,3,1)/8 and (1,9,3,3)/16 over K=0,1,2,3 have the same per-daughter marginal 1/2 and pairwise covariance zero, but different P(K=0) and hence different one-generation clone persistence.
assumptions: Daughter labels are exchangeable conditional on K
K is sampled from the displayed law
claims.status: internally checked exact finite counterexample; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite combinatorial witness illustrating why pairwise covariance is insufficient for b>=3.
claims.costs: No data or code. Empirical identification requires at least the family offspring-count histogram.
claims.falsifier: Direct arithmetic: a failed equality of means/pair moments or unequal exchangeability would falsify this witness.
claims.next_gate: When b>=3, acquire the full offspring-count histogram or PGF rather than only sister-pair correlations.

remaining_control_implication.statement: Ratio-matched synthetic fate controllers should be compared under different fate-resolution timing because identical daughter marginals need not imply identical clone reliability. A recombinase branching platform makes this a plausible assay, but no literature result located here demonstrates independent control of sister dependence at fixed marginals.
remaining_control_implication.status: proposed experimental stress test; not demonstrated actuator and not a novelty claim
